project_comments.note: Cross-cutting review insight: All 6 WPs in this sprint used the captured-closure pattern inside updateWorkPackageWithSync callbacks (claimed, autoFinalizeResult, etc.). This pattern should be standardized with a brief JSDoc convention note in constraints.md so future implementors understand that variables written inside the lock callback and read after the await are correct and safe. Also: propagateDependencyUnblock is absent from both begin-work.ts (WP-003) and auto-finalize in pipeline.ts (WP-006). Both are acceptable for linear workflows but represent a shared architectural gap. A single follow-up WP should export propagateDependencyUnblock from work-package.ts and call it in both completePipeline auto-finalize and beginWork COMPLETE transition paths.

Cross-cutting synthesis: The single highest-priority follow-up from this sprint is the propagateDependencyUnblock gap shared by WP-003 (begin-work.ts COMPLETE transition) and WP-006 (pipeline.ts auto-finalize). Both fast-path completion routes skip the cascade unblock, making dependent WPs invisible to the workflow for projects with non-linear DAGs. A single follow-up WP exporting propagateDependencyUnblock from work-package.ts and calling it in both locations would close this gap completely. All other low-priority observations are cleanup/polish items (stub removal, validatePlanPathOrError migration, eager-loading optimization) suitable for a micro-debt WP.
